title: With Due Respect (Vol. 7) -- Ch. 14: Jose Wright Diokno
keywords: a visionary leader of exemplary integrity
primary_topics: Chapter 14 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7) -- CJP's March 4, 2007 Inquirer column honoring Jose Wright 'Ka Pepe' Diokno on his 85th birthday and 20th death anniversary, presenting him as the living answer to Archbishop Oscar Cruz's challenge to go beyond charity
Cruz's homily -- that loving one's neighbor (Matthew 25) means not only feeding the hungry but also punishing 'the greedy who deprived them of food' -- which CJP found embodied in Diokno

Diokno's standing as the model of 'ethics and competence' (he 'topped both the CPA and the bar' and was admitted without formally graduating) and of 'integrity, not mere honesty' -- having 'the moral courage to punish the greedy, chase the robbers, and prosecute the tyrants'

Diokno's break with Marcos and his detention 'without being charged or tried,' marking him 'a visionary leader of exemplary integrity' -- set among the Bantayog ng mga Bayani heroes, and closing with Salonga's line that 'a nation is measured by the quality of the men and women it honors'
sub_topics: The homily: at a Mass, Archbishop Oscar Cruz preached that the New Testament reduces the commandments to 'love thy God and love thy neighbor,' and that one loves one's neighbor (Matthew 25) by feeding the hungry, clothing the naked and visiting prisoners

Beyond the Gospel: the prelate pressed further -- 'Shall we just feed the hungry but not punish the greedy who deprived them of food?... visit the prisoners without bringing to justice the tyrants who jailed them?' -- questions that, reflecting at home, led CJP to think of Jose W. Diokno

The occasion: Diokno's '85th birthday' (Feb. 26) and '20th death anniversary' (Feb. 27) were marked by De La Salle conferring the '3rd Ka Pepe Diokno Human Rights Award' on Augusto 'Bobbit' Sanchez and launching 'Diokno on Trial' by Jose Manuel Diokno -- and CJP, as keynote speaker, 'remembered him as the answer to Archbishop Cruz's questions'

Ethics and competence: Diokno 'easily exemplified the EC -- ethics and competence' CJP had asked of every lawyer; he 'topped both the CPA and the bar examinations' and, 'with special permission from the Supreme Court,' took the bar 'without having formally graduated from law school' -- a feat that 'remains unsurpassed'

Honest but inert: in an era of officials who 'arrogated absolute power... plundered the treasury, and... amass[ed] ill-gotten wealth,' a 'handful... kept themselves personally pure' yet 'did nothing to stamp out the evil around them,' content to distance themselves -- merely 'honest public servants'

Integrity, not mere honesty: 'honesty is a virtue taught in grade school,' but the country needs 'men and women of integrity' who not only 'refuse to tell a falsehood' but possess 'the moral courage to punish the greedy, chase the robbers, and prosecute the tyrants' -- the same standard CJP urged as Chief Justice

Moral courage: though Diokno 'twice supported the presidential candidacy of... Marcos' (1965 and 1969), he 'did not hesitate to part from him and to denounce his excesses' once Marcos 'was veering away from the straight and narrow' -- risking 'his own safety, health... and career' to 'restore freedom,' for which he was 'incarcerated and kept under solitary confinement without being charged or tried,' proving him 'a visionary leader of exemplary integrity'

The Bantayog and Salonga's measure: asking who else 'measure[s] up to the imperatives of visionary leadership by example,' CJP points to the Bantayog ng mga Bayani heroes -- Ninoy Aquino, Climaco, Concepcion, Javier, Manglapus, Ongpin, JBL Reyes, Sin, Tañada, Teehankee -- 'all... already in the Great Beyond,' and to Bantayog founder Salonga's words that 'a nation is measured by the quality of the men and women it honors,' leaving readers (and the AYLC delegates) to name living leaders worth looking up to

stances.claim: Loving one's neighbor means more than charity -- as Archbishop Cruz pressed, one must also 'punish the greedy who deprived them of food' -- and Jose Diokno was the living answer to that challenge.
stances.rhetorical_move: homily-to-exemplar: answering a preacher's question with a man's life

stances.claim: The country needs 'integrity, not mere honesty' -- not just those who 'refuse to tell a falsehood' but those with 'the moral courage to punish the greedy, chase the robbers, and prosecute the tyrants.'
stances.rhetorical_move: value-distinction: ranking active integrity above passive honesty

stances.claim: Diokno embodied that integrity -- breaking with Marcos at great personal cost and enduring detention 'without being charged or tried' -- making him 'a visionary leader of exemplary integrity,' as a nation 'is measured by the quality of the men and women it honors.'
stances.rhetorical_move: exemplar-and-measure: canonizing Diokno and challenging readers to find living equals

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 14 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7), CJP's March 4, 2007 Inquirer column, honors Jose Wright 'Ka Pepe' Diokno on his 85th birthday and 20th death anniversary, presenting him as the living answer to a homily by Archbishop Oscar Cruz. Cruz preached that loving one's neighbor (Matthew 25) means feeding the hungry and visiting prisoners -- then pressed beyond the Gospel: 'Shall we just feed the hungry but not punish the greedy who deprived them of food?... visit the prisoners without bringing to justice the tyrants who jailed them?' Reflecting at home, CJP thought of Diokno, whose anniversaries De La Salle marked with the 'Ka Pepe Diokno Human Rights Award' and the launch of 'Diokno on Trial.' As keynote speaker, CJP 'remembered him as the answer.' Diokno 'easily exemplified... ethics and competence': he 'topped both the CPA and the bar examinations' and, 'with special permission,' took the bar 'without having formally graduated' -- a feat 'unsurpassed.' In an age of plunderers, CJP distinguishes the merely 'honest public servants' who 'did nothing to stamp out the evil around them' from those of true 'integrity, not mere honesty' -- for 'honesty is a virtue taught in grade school,' but the country needs the 'moral courage to punish the greedy, chase the robbers, and prosecute the tyrants.' Diokno had it: though he 'twice supported the presidential candidacy of... Marcos,' he 'did not hesitate to part from him' and 'denounce his excesses,' risking 'his own safety, health... and career' and enduring 'solitary confinement without being charged or tried' -- 'a visionary leader of exemplary integrity.' Pointing to the Bantayog ng mga Bayani heroes (Ninoy, Climaco, Concepcion, Tañada, Teehankee and more, 'all... in the Great Beyond') and Salonga's words that 'a nation is measured by the quality of the men and women it honors,' CJP leaves readers -- especially the Ayala Young Leaders -- to name the living leaders worth honoring.
